title: Efficient Capital Markets: A Review of Theory and Empirical Work
reported_result: evidence broadly consistent with efficiency conditional on model
main_limitations: joint test of efficiency and asset-pricing model; old microstructure
repository_relevance: sets skeptical prior and benchmark burden
original_concise_summary: Prediction is possible only relative to an information and equilibrium model; abnormal-return claims inherit that joint-test problem.

title: On the Impossibility of Informationally Efficient Markets
authors: Sanford J. Grossman; Joseph E. Stiglitz
reported_result: perfect efficiency is impossible when information is costly
main_limitations: does not identify a tradable empirical signal
original_concise_summary: Prices can be informative without being perfectly revealing because information acquisition must be rewarded.

title: Stock Market Prices Do Not Follow Random Walks: Evidence from a Simple Specification Test
authors: Andrew W. Lo; A. Craig MacKinlay
reported_result: rejects random walk especially for smaller stocks
main_limitations: rejection does not establish net exploitable predictability
original_concise_summary: Statistical departures from a random walk are real in the sample but are not themselves executable alpha.

title: A Comprehensive Look at the Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
cost_assumptions: market-timing utility considered but execution simplified
reported_result: most predictors fail OOS and are unstable
main_limitations: aggregate US evidence may not map to crypto
repository_relevance: directly defines required baselines and skepticism
original_concise_summary: A difficult-to-beat historical-mean forecast exposes how unstable many celebrated return predictors are.

title: Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control
authors: George E. P. Box; Gwilym M. Jenkins
split_validation_design: rolling validation not intrinsic to original method
reported_result: establishes ARIMA identification estimation and diagnostics
main_limitations: linear stationarity and structural instability
repository_relevance: mandatory classical baseline; weak alpha prior
original_concise_summary: ARIMA is a disciplined serial-dependence baseline whose simplicity makes it valuable even when it loses.

title: Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity with Estimates of the Variance of United Kingdom Inflation
reported_result: conditional variance changes predictably
main_limitations: original application is not returns; symmetric response
original_concise_summary: ARCH makes time-varying uncertainty estimable even when the conditional mean is weak.

title: Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity
reported_result: parsimonious persistent volatility dynamics
independent_replication_evidence: extensive; often beaten by realized-volatility models where available
main_limitations: parameter instability; distribution and asymmetry choices
original_concise_summary: GARCH is a compact risk baseline but should not be mistaken for a directional return model.

title: Multivariate Stochastic Variance Models
authors: Andrew C. Harvey; Esther Ruiz; Neil Shephard
reported_result: shows feasible multivariate stochastic-volatility modeling
main_limitations: estimation cost and latent-state uncertainty
repository_relevance: useful benchmark but heavier than HAR
original_concise_summary: Stochastic volatility captures latent common risk but adds estimation complexity without a proven trading payoff here.

title: Modeling and Forecasting Realized Volatility
authors: Torben G. Andersen; Tim Bollerslev; Francis X. Diebold; Paul Labys
dataset_period: roughly a decade of DM/USD and JPY/USD
split_validation_design: chronological volatility forecasts and distributional checks
reported_result: realized volatility supports accurate approximately Gaussian conditional return scaling
main_limitations: microstructure noise and sampling choice
original_concise_summary: High-frequency realized measures make variance forecasting substantially easier than signed-return forecasting.

title: A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility
reported_result: HAR-RV is competitive with more complex long-memory models
independent_replication_evidence: extensive across assets including crypto volatility
main_limitations: bar RV proxy is weaker than high-frequency RV
original_concise_summary: Three causal volatility horizons provide a robust inexpensive approximation to long memory.

title: Co-Integration and Error Correction: Representation Estimation and Testing
authors: Robert F. Engle; Clive W. J. Granger
reported_result: establishes error-correction representation
main_limitations: relation breaks; pretest and selection risk
repository_relevance: relevant to spot/perp spreads with strict break guards
original_concise_summary: A stable long-run relation can support residual forecasts but must be revalidated when venue mechanics change.

title: A New Approach to the Economic Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series and the Business Cycle
split_validation_design: maximum likelihood with filtered and smoothed states
leakage_controls: filtering can be causal; smoothing cannot be used live
reported_result: recovers recession-like regime dynamics
main_limitations: state labels and count are model-dependent
original_concise_summary: Latent regimes are probabilistic states; economic labels require separate evidence and causal filtering.

title: Estimating and Testing Linear Models with Multiple Structural Changes
split_validation_design: global break estimation plus confidence intervals
leakage_controls: offline global estimation is noncausal if misused live
reported_result: provides consistent multiple-break procedures
main_limitations: retrospective breaks do not imply online detection
repository_relevance: use for forensic stability not live alpha
original_concise_summary: Structural-break tests can invalidate a model even when average backtest fit looks acceptable.

title: Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection
authors: Ryan Prescott Adams; David J. C. MacKay
leakage_controls: causal by construction if likelihood inputs are causal
reported_result: tractable posterior over time since last change
main_limitations: hazard and observation model sensitivity
original_concise_summary: Online run-length uncertainty is a principled trigger to distrust a stale forecasting regime.

title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
leakage_controls: lag between formation and holdings in variants
cost_assumptions: period-appropriate trading discussion; incomplete modern impact
reported_result: intermediate-horizon winners outperform losers
independent_replication_evidence: extensive; attenuated after costs/crowding in some periods
main_limitations: equity monthly effect not intraday crypto law
original_concise_summary: Momentum is a cross-sectional portfolio effect whose turnover and crash behavior matter as much as average return.

title: Does the Stock Market Overreact?
authors: Werner F. M. De Bondt; Richard Thaler
split_validation_design: winner/loser formation and later holding periods
reported_result: extreme losers outperform extreme winners later
independent_replication_evidence: mixed after microcap and risk adjustments
main_limitations: microcap liquidity and risk attribution
repository_relevance: mechanism only; repository reversal evidence failed
original_concise_summary: Long-horizon overreaction evidence does not justify short-horizon residual reversal after executable costs.

title: Time Series Momentum
authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse Heje Pedersen
cost_assumptions: cost/capacity discussion; not modern crypto fills
reported_result: positive persistence over 1-12 months with later partial reversal
official_code: author data series available in some forms
main_limitations: horizon and implementation differ from intraday crypto
repository_relevance: strong prior for longer-horizon trend baseline
original_concise_summary: Trend is among the most replicated effects but remains state-dependent and cost-sensitive.

title: Carry
authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen; Tobias J. Moskowitz; Lasse Heje Pedersen; Evert B. Vrugt
instrument_type: currencies; commodities; equities; bonds; credit; options
reported_result: carry comoves across assets and bears global risk
main_limitations: funding rate is not automatically equivalent to carry
repository_relevance: academic origin for prospective carry campaign
original_concise_summary: Carry is an observable yield-like signal but earns compensation for liquidity and crash risks.

title: Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule
authors: Evan Gatev; William N. Goetzmann; K. Geert Rouwenhorst
split_validation_design: formation then trading periods; bootstrap comparisons
cost_assumptions: commissions and conservative execution variants; borrow/impact incomplete
reported_result: reports positive relative-value returns with later weakening
independent_replication_evidence: many replications with lower post-publication returns
main_limitations: selection; relation breaks; borrow; delistings
original_concise_summary: Historical similarity can define a spread but cannot guarantee that the relation survives trading frictions.

title: The Combination of Forecasts
authors: John M. Bates; Clive W. J. Granger
leakage_controls: requires weights based on past errors
reported_result: combinations can beat individual forecasts
main_limitations: unstable covariance and adaptive-weight leakage
repository_relevance: supports bounded ensembles over winner selection
original_concise_summary: Diversification across imperfect forecasts is valuable when weights are learned only from prior errors.

title: Nearest Neighbor Pattern Classification
authors: Thomas M. Cover; Peter E. Hart
reported_result: bounds asymptotic nearest-neighbor error
main_limitations: curse of dimensionality; nonstationary distances
original_concise_summary: Nearest neighbors are transparent but financial similarity metrics decay as regimes and scales move.

title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine
leakage_controls: requires clean split and fitted preprocessing
reported_result: stagewise trees optimize arbitrary differentiable loss
main_limitations: generic method paper gives no financial edge
original_concise_summary: Boosting is a flexible interaction model whose financial value depends on disciplined validation rather than architecture.

title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
authors: Shihao Gu; Bryan Kelly; Dacheng Xiu
split_validation_design: chronological training validation and holdout; portfolio sorts
cost_assumptions: large-cap and turnover analyses; not full impact
reported_result: trees and neural nets improve cross-sectional forecasts; shallow models strong
independent_replication_evidence: substantial follow-up literature with mixed portability
main_limitations: equity breadth and monthly costs differ from crypto perps
original_concise_summary: Nonlinearity helps in a broad panel, but simple structures and economic evaluation remain decisive.

title: Deep Learning with Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Financial Market Predictions
split_validation_design: rolling train/test comparison against RF; DNN; logistic
cost_assumptions: 5 bp per half turn in reported trading test
reported_result: LSTM leads full sample but edge decays materially late and after costs
independent_replication_evidence: many ML finance studies; fragile net replication
main_limitations: constituent and tuning bias; simplified execution
repository_relevance: current LSTM is architectural but validation/provenance gaps remain
original_concise_summary: A real LSTM can win an old sample and still fail the later economically relevant regime.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling
authors: Shaojie Bai; J. Zico Kolter; Vladlen Koltun
reported_result: TCNs often outperform canonical recurrent networks on benchmarks
main_limitations: not a financial/economic study
repository_relevance: defines fidelity gap for repository TCN proxy
original_concise_summary: Dilated lag features alone are not a temporal convolutional network with learned causal kernels and residual blocks.

title: Attention Is All You Need
input_data: embedded tokens; positional encodings; multi-head attention
reported_result: Transformer improves translation quality and parallelism
main_limitations: no market validation
repository_relevance: defines fidelity gap for similarity proxy
original_concise_summary: Softmax similarity to stored targets is not a projected multi-head Transformer.

title: Temporal Fusion Transformers for Interpretable Multi-horizon Time Series Forecasting
reported_result: competitive multihorizon forecasts with variable-selection diagnostics
independent_replication_evidence: broad forecasting replication; finance alpha unproven
main_limitations: large architecture and known-future covariate assumptions
original_concise_summary: Interpretable attention and quantiles are useful, but benchmark forecast gains do not establish net trading value.

title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers
leakage_controls: patches drawn from past context; channel independence
reported_result: strong long-horizon benchmark performance
main_limitations: no costs or finance; benchmark controversies
repository_relevance: current identifier is a ridge patch-summary proxy
original_concise_summary: The paper's core is patch-token self-attention with channel independence, which the repository does not implement.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research / arXiv
input_data: scaled and quantized values plus synthetic series
reported_result: competitive zero-shot forecasts; strongest on seen or related domains
main_limitations: pretraining overlap; model size; no net finance evidence
original_concise_summary: A transferable probabilistic prior is interesting, but its general forecast loss is not evidence of executable crypto alpha.

title: A Decoder-only Foundation Model for Time-series Forecasting
input_data: patched history; large real and synthetic corpus
dataset_period: about 100 billion pretraining points plus public benchmarks
reported_result: near supervised benchmark performance zero-shot
main_limitations: memory footprint; pretraining opacity; no trading costs
original_concise_summary: TimesFM reduces per-series training but replaces it with a large opaque dependency that has no proven trading payoff here.

title: GIFT-Eval: A Benchmark for General Time Series Forecasting Model Evaluation
leakage_controls: pretraining dataset designed to avoid evaluation leakage
reported_result: model rankings vary by dataset and horizon
main_limitations: little market microstructure and no economic metric
original_concise_summary: A broad benchmark is valuable chiefly because it shows no foundation model is universally dominant.

title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
authors: Rama Cont; Arseniy Kukanov; Sasha Stoikov
leakage_controls: event ordering retained; causal forecasting distinction limited
reported_result: price change is linearly related to OFI; impact inversely related to depth
main_limitations: main result is partly contemporaneous; queue/fill gap
repository_relevance: strong mechanism but missing required data
original_concise_summary: Depth-normalized OFI is a credible microstructure feature only when event timing and fills are modeled faithfully.

title: Universal Features of Price Formation in Financial Markets: Perspectives from Deep Learning
input_data: raw order-book states pooled across assets
dataset_period: very large US equity event sample
reported_result: pooled models learn stable cross-asset price-formation features
independent_replication_evidence: follow-up microstructure literature supports pooled learning
main_limitations: accuracy-to-fill and latency gap
repository_relevance: supports pooled challenger only after L2 archive
original_concise_summary: Cross-asset book regularities exist, but their horizon is too short to ignore latency and adverse selection.

title: DeepLOB: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Limit Order Books
authors: Zihao Zhang; Stefan Zohren; Stephen Roberts
split_validation_design: anchored chronological folds on FI-2010 plus transfer tests
leakage_controls: chronological protocol improved over random split
reported_result: CNN-LSTM architecture improves classification benchmarks
independent_replication_evidence: replication sensitive to labels and evaluation protocol
data_license: FI-2010 public research terms; others restricted
main_limitations: benchmark leakage concerns; no queue economics
original_concise_summary: Book-classification accuracy is not a fillable edge and requires data the repository does not retain.

title: Deep Order Flow Imbalance: Extracting Alpha at Multiple Horizons from the Limit Order Book
authors: Petter N. Kolm; Jeremy Turiel; Nicholas Westray
forecast_horizon: a few price changes to longer event horizons
input_data: stationary order-flow features and raw book
cost_assumptions: economic conversion discussed but queue/impact remain
reported_result: stationary OFI features outperform raw states; useful horizon is very short
main_limitations: equity data; latency; restricted data
original_concise_summary: Feature stationarity matters more than architecture, but execution dominates at the reported horizon.

title: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
leakage_controls: lagged predictors; timing details vary by source
cost_assumptions: turnover and implementation costs not comprehensive
reported_result: network growth; momentum; attention forecast returns; production proxies weak
main_limitations: short early sample; revisions and many predictors
original_concise_summary: Crypto-specific momentum and attention are plausible but require first-seen timestamps and later-period replication.

title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
authors: Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski; Xi Wu
split_validation_design: portfolio sorts; factor spanning; subperiod analyses
cost_assumptions: tradability filters and costs considered but not venue-level fills
reported_result: market size and momentum factors span ten successful characteristics
independent_replication_evidence: replication code available; later portability still uncertain
main_limitations: survivorship; exchange fragmentation; investability
repository_relevance: best support for true PIT ranker
original_concise_summary: A broad point-in-time universe is essential because crypto factor evidence is cross-sectional rather than a single-asset timing rule.

title: Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
cost_assumptions: capital transfer and settlement frictions central
reported_result: large persistent international price differences reflect segmented capital
independent_replication_evidence: widely cited with continued fragmentation evidence
main_limitations: custody transfer and counterparty constraints
repository_relevance: supports cross-venue context not easy arbitrage
original_concise_summary: Cross-exchange spreads persist precisely because capital and settlement constraints make them costly to capture.

title: A Reality Check for Data Snooping
reported_result: many apparent winners lose significance after data-snooping correction
main_limitations: requires complete trial family and valid bootstrap
original_concise_summary: The search process is part of the hypothesis and must be tested rather than hidden behind the winning configuration.

title: A Test for Superior Predictive Ability
venue: Journal of Business and Economic Statistics
split_validation_design: studentized bootstrap and treatment of poor alternatives
reported_result: improves power over Reality Check in relevant settings
main_limitations: bootstrap dependence and family completeness
repository_relevance: candidate for future formal campaign tests
original_concise_summary: SPA asks whether any searched model truly beats the benchmark while reducing dilution from obviously poor alternatives.

title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
authors: David H. Bailey; Marcos López de Prado
split_validation_design: analytical correction relative to expected maximum Sharpe
cost_assumptions: costs must already be in returns
reported_result: conventional Sharpe confidence is overstated after selection
independent_replication_evidence: widely used; implementation details sometimes vary
main_limitations: cannot fix omitted trials leakage or wrong costs
original_concise_summary: DSR is a confidence gate over net returns, not a replacement for causal data and complete trial accounting.

title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
authors: David H. Bailey; Jonathan Borwein; Marcos López de Prado; Qiji Jim Zhu
cost_assumptions: costs must already be in returns
reported_result: quantifies likelihood that in-sample winner underperforms OOS
independent_replication_evidence: growing use; sensitive to implementation and sample
main_limitations: needs complete finite aligned matrix and enough observations
original_concise_summary: PBO reveals whether the selection rule repeatedly chooses candidates that reverse rank out of sample.

title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
split_validation_design: original sample vs post-sample vs post-publication
reported_result: returns are about 26 percent lower OOS and 58 percent lower after publication
main_limitations: equity anomaly publication process differs from crypto
original_concise_summary: Predictability decays both because original results overfit and because publication changes markets.

title: Replicating Anomalies
authors: Kewei Hou; Chen Xue; Lu Zhang
leakage_controls: common definitions; value weighting; higher t hurdle
cost_assumptions: liquidity addressed through value weighting; costs incomplete
reported_result: 65 percent fail value-weighted replication and 82 percent fail higher hurdle
independent_replication_evidence: major independent replication project; debated definitions
main_limitations: design choices affect anomaly identity
repository_relevance: supports strict gates and negative outcomes
original_concise_summary: Uniform implementation and multiplicity-aware hurdles eliminate most nominal anomalies.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
input_data: past conformity scores and adaptive level
reported_result: achieves long-run coverage adaptation under arbitrary shift formulation
independent_replication_evidence: large follow-up literature; conditional coverage remains hard
main_limitations: coverage alone can be uninformative if intervals widen; dependent finance data
original_concise_summary: Adaptive coverage is useful only when interval width and abstention economics remain acceptable.

title: Exploring Risk and Return Profiles of Funding Rate Arbitrage on CEX and DEX
cost_assumptions: fees/leverage considered; cross-venue fill and failure details limited
reported_result: reports selected return up to 115.9 percent over six months with 1.92 percent drawdown
main_limitations: multiple scenarios; leverage; venue and liquidation fidelity
repository_relevance: new mechanism evidence but insufficient replication
original_concise_summary: The attractive selected funding scenario is a hypothesis generator because execution and multiple testing remain unresolved.

title: Anatomy of Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures Returns
authors: Yi Cao; Pengfei Luo; Yuhan Cheng; Yizhe Dong
input_data: basis; momentum; liquidity; size; volatility; price-volume
reported_result: reports 63 significant sorts and a log-basis/price-volume factor explanation
main_limitations: one-page posting; severe multiplicity and missing methods
original_concise_summary: A broad predictor horse race without full protocol and independent replication cannot clear the repository's evidence gate.

title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
input_data: informed orders; noise trading; market-maker inference
reported_result: derives linear price impact and gradual information release
main_limitations: stylized single-asset equilibrium
repository_relevance: basis for adverse-selection and impact requirements
original_concise_summary: Order size moves prices because market makers infer information from flow; impact cannot be omitted from capacity claims.

title: Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions
venue: Journal of Risk / Journal of Portfolio Management reference
reported_result: efficient frontier trades expected cost against execution risk
main_limitations: linear/quadratic impact and calibration assumptions
original_concise_summary: A signal has no economic value until its order schedule survives the cost-risk frontier.

title: Variance Risk Premia
leakage_controls: implied measure at observation time; realized outcome later
reported_result: documents large negative variance risk premium and its dynamics
independent_replication_evidence: extensive across equity and other options
main_limitations: options data and instrument mechanics absent in repo
original_concise_summary: Implied minus realized variance contains risk-premium information but needs licensed surfaces and options-aware execution.
